title: Replace monolithic model loader with pluggable shard adapters and lexicon gateway
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Background: The current model ingestion path is a single large loader that handles checkpoint discovery, weight deserialization, shard reassembly and tokenizer initialization. Over time this monolith has accumulated special-case logic for legacy checkpoint variants, ad-hoc sharding heuristics, and multiple tokenizer init flows. This has increased maintenance cost, caused inconsistent startup latency across model variants, and made targeted upgrades (e.g., introducing a new checkpoint schema or tokenizer runtime) risky.

This ticket replaces the monolithic loader with a pluggable shard adapter framework plus a small lexicon gateway that centralizes tokenizer contracts. Goals: 1) introduce a stable checkpoint manifest contract and adapter interface so format-specific logic lives in isolated modules, 2) provide a shard activation coordinator that supports partial activation/fallback and parallel piecemeal hydration, 3) unify tokenizer init through a lexicon gateway that exposes a versioned tokenizer API to the runtime, and 4) reduce median model load time and 99th percentile activation tail.

Scope: implement adapter interface, migrate two representative legacy checkpoint formats to adapters, implement lexicon gateway shim, add activation metrics, and ship a canary rollout for a small set of nightly models. Migration will be reversible with a runtime toggle for 3 weeks.

Out of scope: changing low-level kernel selection, weight quantization strategies, or full rework of distributed checkpoint streaming protocol (those will be tracked as follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a documented adapter interface (IShardAdapter) with unit tests and type annotations
At least two legacy checkpoint formats are implemented as adapters and pass existing model compatibility tests
Lexicon gateway implemented with a single tokenizer API and backward-compatible adapter layer for old tokenizer initializers
End-to-end canary: 50% of nightly small transformer models load via new path with no increase in error rate and an observed median startup time reduction of >= 12%
Add dashboard panels for model_load_time, activation_99p_tail, shard_activation_success_rate, tokenizer_init_time
Rollback toggle validated in staging and documented in runbook
technical_notes: Adapter design: lightweight module with methods: detect_manifest, stream_shard, verify_checksum, provide_metadata. Adapters must be loadable via entry points to avoid runtime rebuilds.

Shard activation coordinator: supports parallel fetch of independent shards and an atomic activation step once required KV sets are present. Will allow partial activation + graceful degradation to smaller context lengths until full activation completes.

Lexicon gateway: single process-local API that returns tokenizer handles by (model_id, tokenizer_version). Gateway will memoize per-worker tokenizers and provide compatibility wrappers for legacy tokenizers.
Compatibility: maintain existing manifest lookups; new manifest fields optional so older adapters still workable. Use feature-flagged schema checks before enabling strict validation.
Metrics: instrument with histogram for tokenizer_init_time, timers for shard_stream_duration, counter for adapter_failures. Tag metrics by adapter_type and model_family.

Testing: add integration harness (pytest) that spins a memory-only shard store to simulate partial shards and compares outputs pre/post migration. Include fuzz of corrupted shard segments to validate fallback behavior.
Performance targets: reduce median model_load_time for medium-sized models (<= 7B) from baseline 1.8s to <= 1.6s; reduce activation_99p_tail by at least 20% for pipelined activations.
Migration plan: implement adapters behind FEATURE_FLAG_NEW_LOADER. Stage rollout: dev -> staging -> canary (nightly models) -> 50% traffic -> full. Each stage gated by metrics and error budgets.
Rollout concerns: ensure GC/heap pressure is monitored as memoized tokenizers increase per-worker memory. Add eviction policy to lexicon gateway (LRU with max-memory cap).
Documentation: Confluence doc 'Model Loader: adapter contract and lexicon gateway' with code samples and diagnostics.

Risk: potential for subtle tokenization divergence. We'll include token-level diff tests on a corpus of 50 prompts across model families to detect regressions before enabling the flag for user traffic.
updates: 2026-02-12: RFC drafted and posted to eng-channel. High-level design reviewed in Arch sync. Action: Pratt to prototype adapter loader.
2026-02-25: Prototype adapter loader implemented; early perf numbers show 8% median improvement for small test models. Tokenizer gateway sketch done.
2026-03-03: Security reviewed memo: no additional KMS changes required; gateway runs in same process. Noted memory trade-offs; added LRU eviction requirement.
2026-03-08: Integration tests added. Found tokenization mismatch for legacy BPE variant; created compatibility wrapper in adapter-legacy-bpe. Added token-diff test cases.

2026-03-12: Canary rollout scheduled for nightly models tomorrow. PR #1842 requires one more review from runtime/reliability. Measured activation_99p_tail decrease of ~22% in staging for pipelined models.
